assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiencies from a few percent to well above 25 percent within about a decade, a rare case of a crystalline material family whose composition-structure-property relations (tolerance factor, defect tolerance, tunable band gap) explain the function. Large, lasting impact on photovoltaics, tandem cells and optoelectronics.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers; Park and Snaith made the decisive step to solid-state, thin-film devices with high efficiency and stability improvements. Kanatzidis and Grätzel also have strong claims, so a three-person cut is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced worldwide and commercially pursued, but long-term operational stability, lead content and scale-up remain open, so some may judge recognition slightly early.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Miyasaka, Snaith, Park, Seok, Grätzel and Kanatzidis is unresolved.
Long-term device stability under real operating conditions is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The identification and structural characterization of multi-walled and single-walled carbon nanotubes by HRTEM and electron diffraction opened a whole field of nanocarbon materials. Originality and clarity are high, and structure (chirality, helicity) directly explains electronic properties. Very strong lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Iijima's 1991 Nature paper with HRTEM and diffraction evidence is the widely recognized origin; Bethune and Endo contributed single-wall synthesis and earlier filament observations, but Iijima is the clearest single laureate. Earlier priority claims for hollow carbon filaments exist.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent confirmation and applications in composites and electronics; recognition is overdue rather than premature, though the 1996 fullerene prize covers adjacent ground and some may see it as physics-leaning.
uncertainties: Prior observations of hollow carbon filaments complicate priority.
Whether the committee sees the topic as sufficiently chemical, given the 1996 fullerene prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Crystal structures of the Mo-Fe protein, the discovery of the interstitial carbide in the FeMo cofactor and structures of turnover-relevant states address how nature reduces dinitrogen. Fundamental, clear structural chemistry with major implications for catalysis and fertilizer chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first structures and led the cofactor work; Einsle contributed the atomic-resolution structure revealing the central light atom; Seefeldt and Dean contributed mechanism and genetics; Ribbe also contributed. Credit is distributed and a three-person cut would leave out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed over decades, but the catalytic mechanism, substrate-binding site and the E4 state details remain actively debated, so mechanistic interpretation is not fully stable.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 binding and reduction is not settled.
Credit allocation among Dean, Seefeldt, Ribbe, Rees and Einsle is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves with controlled pore architecture, organic structure-directing agents and tailored active sites underlies refining, emissions control and fine chemicals. Structure determination (including by electron diffraction) is central to the field, and impact is industrially huge.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design and application), Zones (SDA-driven synthesis of industrial zeolites such as SSZ-13) and Davis (zeolite synthesis and structure-property control) are plausible; Yu, Tsapatsis and others also contributed. Credit is diffuse and the work is a long accumulation rather than a single discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature and industrially validated, but because the prize cluster is a broad field with gradual advances, the specific discovery is less sharply defined and the 2025 framework-materials prize overlaps in spirit.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit across a broad field.
Possible perceived overlap with the 2025 framework-materials recognition.
I have a professional interest in this field and should weigh that carefully.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography uses XFEL pulses to collect diffraction from micro- and nanocrystals before radiation damage, enabling room-temperature and time-resolved structures of membrane proteins and reaction intermediates. An enabling method that let a community see what it could not before, directly related to nanocrystal structure determination.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the conceptual and experimental development with Fromme and Schlichting contributing key protein and time-resolved applications; Hajdu originated the diffract-before-destroy concept. Hajdu's omission from a three-person set is a real cost.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed at several XFEL facilities and increasingly routine, though the field is still evolving with synchrotron serial methods and time-resolved chemistry; reasonably mature but not fully settled.
uncertainties: Allocation between Hajdu, Chapman, Fromme and Schlichting.
How much of the impact is methodological versus chemical insight.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silica (M41S, SBA-15, MCM-41) created a new class of porous solids with tunable pores of 2 to 50 nm, supporting catalysis, adsorption, nanocasting and hard-templating. Original, clearly demonstrated and broadly influential in materials chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) made the original discovery; Ryoo extended to ordered mesoporous carbons and nanocasting; Zhao and Stucky developed SBA-15 and related syntheses. Choosing among Mobil team members and later contributors is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Well established for decades; peak excitement has passed, and applications are more limited than for zeolites, which may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Priority within the Mobil team and between original and follow-on discoveries.
Whether impact is deemed sufficiently large relative to other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the delivery technology that made siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines practical, with enormous demonstrated medical impact. The science combines lipid chemistry, self-assembly and structure-activity design.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the lipid nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid concepts; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid and delivery libraries; others such as MacLachlan, Hope and Madden made key contributions. Boundaries with the 2023 medicine prize and with patent disputes complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: Validated clinically at scale; timing is favorable, but the chemistry is more pharmaceutical and the structure-function understanding of the particles is still incomplete.
uncertainties: Complex credit allocation among many contributors and institutions.
Fit with the chemistry prize versus medicine, which already recognized mRNA vaccines.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts, proven by aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM and X-ray absorption, offer maximal atom efficiency and well-defined active sites that bridge homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis. Strong structural-evidence base and growing application.
assessment.attribution: Zhang and Qiao's 2011 Pt1/FeOx paper coined the concept and demonstrated catalytic relevance; Liu contributed the microscopy characterization. Datye, Wang and Li also contributed, and earlier single-site work complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Still maturing: debates about stability, loading, true coordination environment and reproducibility of claimed single-atom structures persist, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Distinguishing true single-atom sites from clusters depends on careful characterization.
Priority relative to earlier single-site and supported-organometallic catalysts.
